title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
why: Origin of SAM; every subsequent SAM paper cites this.

title: Towards Understanding Sharpness-Aware Minimization
why: Argues SAM's benefit is NOT explained by flatness alone; load-bearing counterargument for the RQ.

title: How Does Sharpness-Aware Minimization Minimize Sharpness?
why: Theoretical decomposition of SAM's actual update; key for mechanism discussion.

title: ASAM: Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Scale-Invariant Learning of Deep Neural Networks
why: Key SAM variant addressing scale invariance; often cited as immediate successor.

title: Normalization Layers Are All That Sharpness-Aware Minimization Needs
why: Empirical decomposition showing SAM's effect localises to normalization layers; mechanism evidence.

title: On Large-Batch Training for Deep Learning: Generalization Gap and Sharp Minima
why: Empirical foundation of the flat-minima-generalises hypothesis.

title: Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets
why: Counterargument: sharpness is reparametrisation-dependent; must be addressed in Related Work.

title: Fantastic Generalization Measures and Where to Find Them
why: Large-scale empirical comparison of generalisation measures; finds sharpness predictive.

title: Relative Flatness and Generalization
why: Reparametrisation-invariant flatness measure; addresses Dinh's critique.

title: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations
why: Defines CIFAR-C / ImageNet-C; the OOD evaluation target.

title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
why: Calibration under shift; anchors the ECE metric in the experiment.

title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
why: DomainBed framing; argues most DG methods don't beat ERM under fair eval. Methodological discipline.

title: SWAD: Domain Generalization by Seeking Flat Minima
why: Most direct prior on flatness-for-DG; uses weight averaging variant.

title: Sharpness-Aware Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization
why: Recent SAM-for-DG; positions our work against SOTA.

title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
why: SWA origin; the flat-minima-oriented control baseline.

title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited
